svg.title: KEM results: which combiner survives which failure
svg.text: KEM results: which combiner survives which failure
Rows: what was broken on purpose. Columns: five ways to combine the two keys, each attacked in seven games.
Exactly one component failed (failure model · which component)
no attack found (not a proof of security)
Outlined: VYRA with exactly one failed component. 0 of 70 squares broken (230 cells, 200 trials each).
A square is BROKEN if any coded attacker for that game won. Components: ML-KEM-512 and HQC-128. K-CT and K-PK are the key-binding games (HON, LEAK, MAL:
honest, leaked or attacker-chosen secret keys). VYRA breaks only when both components lose confidentiality, where nothing is left to protect.
